Bug_Title: Assertions should not be used in production code
Bug_Details:
Assertions are intended to be used in test code, but not in production code. It is confusing, and might lead to ClassNotFoundException when the build tools only provide the required dependency in test scope.
In addition, assertions will throw a sub-class of Error : AssertionError , which should be avoided in production code.
This rule raises an issue when any assertion intended to be used in test is used in production code.
Supported frameworks:
JUnit FestAssert AssertJ
JUnit
FestAssert
AssertJ
Note: this does not apply for assert from Java itself or if the source code package name is related to tests (contains: test or assert or junit ).
Bug_Explanation: The code uses Java assertions in production code, which can lead to AssertionError and is intended only for testing purposes. Assertions should not be used in production as they might be disabled at runtime.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test cases trigger the bug by calling the 'showBug' method with a negative number, which causes the assertion to fail and throw an AssertionError. This demonstrates the inappropriate use of assertions in production code, as outlined in the bug rule.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that all tests passed successfully without any errors. This indicates that the assertions in the production code did not cause any failures, and thus the presence of the bug was not confirmed by the test run results.
